verses.text: Thank the LORD! Call on his name! Tell the nations what he has done.
Sing to him! Sing praises to him! Tell about all the amazing things he has done.
Be proud of his holy name. Let the hearts of those who look for the LORD be glad.
Look to the LORD and his strength. Always look for his face.
Remember the amazing things he has done, his miracles and the judgments he spoke,
you descendants of his servant Abraham, you children of Jacob, his chosen people.
He is the LORD our God. His judgments are over all the earth.
He remembers his covenant forever, the promise he made for a thousand generations.
It is the covenant he made with Abraham, the promise he made to Isaac.
He confirmed it to Jacob as a law, to Israel as a covenant that lasts forever.
He said, "I will give you the land of Canaan as your share, as your own property."
At that time there were only a few of them, very few, and they were strangers in the land.
They wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another.
He did not let anyone treat them badly. He warned kings because of them:
"Do not touch my anointed ones! Do not harm my prophets!"
He called for a famine on the land and destroyed all their food supplies.
He sent a man ahead of them, Joseph, who was sold as a slave.
They hurt his feet with chains, and his neck was put in irons,
until what he had predicted came true, and the LORD's word proved him right.
The king sent for him and set him free. The ruler of nations let him go.
He put him in charge of his household and made him ruler over everything he owned,
to give orders to his officials as he pleased and to teach his advisers wisdom.
Then Israel came to Egypt. Jacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.
The LORD made his people grow in number and made them stronger than their enemies.
He turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people, to plot against his servants.
He sent his servant Moses, and Aaron, whom he had chosen.
They did his miraculous signs among the Egyptians, his wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness and made the land dark. They did not rebel against his words.
He turned their water into blood and made their fish die.
Their land was overrun with frogs, even in the bedrooms of their kings.
He spoke, and swarms of flies came, and gnats filled their whole country.
He gave them hail instead of rain, with lightning flashing across their land.
He destroyed their grapevines and fig trees and smashed the trees all over their country.
He spoke, and locusts came, and grasshoppers too many to count.
They ate every plant in their land and ate up all their crops.
Then he struck down all the firstborn sons in their land, the first children of their strength.
He brought Israel out, loaded with silver and gold. No one among his tribes stumbled.
Egypt was glad when they left, because the Egyptians were terrified of them.
He spread out a cloud to cover them and gave them fire to light up the night.
They asked, and he brought them quails. He satisfied them with bread from heaven.
He split open the rock, and water gushed out. It flowed like a river in the desert.
He remembered his holy promise to his servant Abraham.
He brought his people out with joy, his chosen ones with shouts of happiness.
He gave them the lands of the nations. They took over what others had worked for,
so they would keep his laws and obey his teachings. Praise the LORD!
